summary: Deocar Schmid (1791–1828) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the University of Jena from 1808 to 1813 under Carl Christian Erhard Schmid.

Derek F. Maher works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has held teaching posts at Virginia, UNC Greensboro, and East Carolina University.

Dermot Killingley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Merton College, Oxford, and SOAS under David Friedman and Arnold Kunst. He taught at the University of Malaya and was a Reader at Newcastle University (~1970–2000).

Dermott Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed a BA at Trinity College Dublin, an MA at Leiden University, and a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, supervised by William M. Bodiford.

Dessislava Vendova specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Sofia University, BLCU, Peking University, Kyoto University, and Columbia University, she has held appointments at NYU, the Graduate Theological Union, MFA Boston, UMass Boston, and College of the Holy Cross.

Detlef Ingo Lauf (1936–2001) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at the C. G. Jung Institute Zürich, the California Institute of Integral Studies, Ohio University, and Columbia Pacific University.

Devachandra Bharati 'Prakhar' works in Buddhist and religious studies. He became a research scholar at Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Rohilkhand University in 2021 and pursued his Ph.D. there from 2021 to 2026.

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of India's Western Circle (1911–1917) and Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910).

Devendra Nath Ojha is an Indologist who completed a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Delhi (2011–2013) and earned a certificate from National Sanskrit University (2020). In 2017, he became HoD Sanskrit and Assistant Professor at Amity University.
Devesh Soneji is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He held a post at the University of Manitoba (attested 1996–1997) and later served as a professor at McGill University (attested 1999).
Deviprasad Mishra is an Indologist who earned his PhD in 1999 at the French Institute of Pondicherry, where he also served as Deputy Head of Indology and researcher.
Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under teachers including Gaton Ngawang Lekpa and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and worked on a research project at the University of Washington (1960–1972).

Dhananjay Vashistha works in Indology and philosophy. After earning a B.E. from BITS Pilani (2011–2015) and working at Cisco Systems and Trans IAS Academy, he became a Research Associate at the Bhaktivedanta Research Center in 2023.

Dharm P. S. Bhawuk is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1992–1995) and was appointed Affiliate Faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 1995.

Dharmananda Kosambi (1876–1947) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Harvard (1926) and held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1906–1908), Harvard (~1910–1932), Gujarat University (~1920–1928), and Saint Petersburg State University (~1929–1931).

Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held appointments at Patna College in 1928 and the University of Minnesota Twin Cities from 1951 to 1952.
Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He has held teaching posts at the Open University, University of Leeds, University of Bristol, and University of Chester.
